prediction.likelyOutcome: Can IV is favored to establish that the bankruptcy filing triggered full recourse under the guaranty, and the prior Washtenaw/bankruptcy court findings of borrower mismanagement undercut Schubiner's 'lender caused the default' narrative. The case will likely turn on whether Schubiner's guarantor-discharge defenses (material alteration via the court-sanctioned receiver loan; misapplication of the $75M credit bid) survive summary disposition — Can IV should be favored there too given the judicial sanction of the receivership, but a genuine triable issue exists. Schubiner's DACA counterclaim is a real but close question; his broader lender-liability/breach counterclaim is weak given prior adverse findings against Packard Square on essentially the same theory.

outcome.description: On cross-motions, the trial court granted summary disposition to the lender on its guaranty claim and on Schubiner's counterclaims and on December 17, 2019 entered judgment against him for $13,992,936.05 (the original-loan balance left after the lender applied its $75 million credit bid first to the receiver loan), plus attorney fees, consultant fees, continuing interest and costs. The Court of Appeals affirmed the judgment (Docket No. 352510), while vacating a separate postjudgment order on intervenors' properties.
